name: Hip thrust
angleNote: Hip flexion: 0° = hips fully up (body straight from shoulders to knees), 80° = hips down. Lifting makes the angle smaller. Torques are per leg.

strength.note: Relative hip-extension torque vs hip flexion, assumed strongest with the hip bent. Peak is per leg, typical trained adult. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

strength.note: Relative knee-extension torque vs knee flexion, weakest near straight, strongest around 60°. Peak is per leg. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

strength.note: Relative plantarflexion torque, strongest with the calf stretched. Peak is per leg. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

muscles.name: Gluteus maximus
muscles.note: Main hip extensor, working hardest at full hip extension.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.note: Extend the hip; with the knee bending at the same time they change length little, so they help less in squats than in hinges.

muscles.name: Adductor magnus
muscles.note: Rear part extends the hip, more so when it is deeply bent.

muscles.name: Quadriceps
muscles.note: Knee extensors: their share follows the knee torque.

phases.name: Top
phases.text: Hips up: the bar's moment arm about the hips is set by where the bench and feet carry the load.

phases.name: Bottom
phases.text: Hips down: the trunk tilts and more weight rests on the bench.

variants.name: Barbell hip thrust
variants.equipment: Barbell, upper back on a bench
variants.notes: Upper back on a bench, feet flat, bar across the hips. The bench and the floor push straight up; how much each carries follows from balance. The knee torque shows the quads also work.

variants.name: Barbell hip thrust, feet further away
variants.equipment: Barbell, upper back on a bench
variants.notes: Feet further from the bench: less knee bend, the knee torque shifts towards flexion (hamstrings) and the hips keep their load.

variants.name: Glute bridge
variants.notes: Shoulders on the floor: a much shorter range of hip motion (try 0–35°).
